# Test data

The top-level protocol JSONL files are handwritten, synthetic lifecycle
examples from the source repository. Their identifiers are test identifiers;
their four zero PCM bytes contain no speech. The synthetic Moshi JSONL file is
generated by `replay_fixture.py` and encodes capabilities, not model behavior.

`replay_fixture.py` generates a deterministic oscillator WAV and protocol events
in a caller-selected ignored directory. No real voice recordings are packaged.
Historical model-output recordings were excluded because a synthetic label
alone does not establish redistribution rights for generated voices.

Example: `python -m tests.fixtures.replay_fixture --backend modular --output artifacts/replay-fixture`.
Replay and mock checks establish client/protocol behavior only, never real
inference performance, recognition quality or audible conversation quality.
